turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's zero was in the gradebook before anyone called me.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
"What we found." Who is "we", and what exactly did you find? I'm writing this down.
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.

"The night before it was due" is when a file was opened, Hale, not who wrote it or how. Owen works twenty hours a week and leaves things late like every Grade 12 student I know. What else do you have, or is that it?
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
I'm writing down 11:52, 612 words, 11:58, 794. A paste moves text from somewhere to somewhere, Hale, and you haven't told me where from. Show me the history itself, with the dates on it.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked to see the history, with the dates on it.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.

I'm writing down "three editions." A student misquoting a line from memory is a mistake, Hale, and mistakes don't get a zero. Which three editions, and show me the page of the essay where the line is.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Then why are we here, Hale? You still haven't shown me the editions or the page.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.

October 15, I'm writing that down. A student changing his mind between an outline and a final draft is called writing an essay, Hale. Did anyone ask Owen about any of this before the zero went in, and where is that outline?
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, Hale, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Your own procedure says the same in 4.3. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
You're asking me how to do your job, Hale? There is no off the record in this room. Withdraw the zero, or answer my question about Owen.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

I'm writing down "supervised rewrite" and "nothing on his record." Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, and I want it in an email from you tonight. I'm still waiting on the history, the outline and the editions, Hale, and I'm still waiting for an answer about Owen.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? Ten minutes, Hale. Owen's record, the editions, the history, and an answer about whether anyone spoke to him.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

You're giving me an ultimatum, Hale, and I haven't refused anything. I've asked for the zero to come off and for your documents in front of me. If it stands, I'm in the principal's office today, not "Monday."
So. Rewrite, or zero?
The zero comes off, Hale. Then we talk about a rewrite, private, with a written promise that nothing goes on file. Put the history and the outline on this desk first.
